title: Lesson 2: Service Lines, Offers, and Packaging
description: How a practice turns capability into something a client can actually buy. The difference between a service line and an offer, why packaging is the principal's real product work, and how productization fixes the worst economics in consulting.

questions.explanation: The lesson is centered on: How a practice turns capability into something a client can actually buy. The difference between a service line and an offer, why packaging is the principal's real product work, and how productization fixes the worst economics in consulting.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the lesson’s guidance?
options: They have capability, which nobody can buy, and no offers, which are the only things a client can buy.
That frame stays abstract until the practice has something to sell, and most practices fail exactly there.
A principal sells capacity, wins through leverage, and builds the delivery system rather than the deliverables.
It teaches you to split what you do into service lines, turn each line into priced offers, and package those offers so a client can buy them without you inventing the scope from scratch every time.
